body:
Can you explain these in a bit more detail?
- The first suggestion doesn't make sense to me. What does it mean?
- For the second suggestion, what do you mean by "record"? Do you mean log it to the console? If so, and two browsers already do, then we should just update the spec to do so. (See also #35)
- The third suggestion sounds like something no browsers do today, so it might be worth opening as a feature request to see if you can get implementer interest. I am not so sure implementers would be interested in this though since it would make pages that previously have a silent console start spewing messages, which would be surprising to developers.
- The fourth suggestion doesn't seem observable, since the log levels only impact presentational things; e.g. Chrome conflates most log levels together.

> The first suggestion doesn't make sense to me. What does it mean?

In a higher level, I would like to have access to this register after I call `.assert` n times.

> For the second suggestion, what do you mean by "record"? Do you mean log it to the console? If so, and two browsers already do, then we should just update the spec to do so. (See also #35)

"print a stack trace" would be a better terminology than "record", as suggested on #35.

> The third suggestion sounds like something no browsers do today

yes, and that's why the fourth suggestion might be useful to avoid any undesired excessive log messages

On the fourth suggestion, I wonder if we could figure out a way to use an `assert` log level to be used specially for assertions, with a special conditional to tell success or fail results, so the printer can handle how they are treated.

> Chrome conflates most log levels together.

As in node which apparently uses stdout and stderr only. Even though, that allows other views to categorize these special cases.

Thanks for the feedback. I know most of these are feature requests and need more work to become a true feature proposal. Count me in for any help to the progress of this spec.
